report:
Reviewed the complete external_identity claim, both ordinary implementation entries (SymExt and the newly associated rustc definition-kind adapter), and the sole associated TODO test. Requirements: external dependency identity is its crate number and definition index, independent of which metadata facts are requested; adapters must supply one consistent definition kind for that identity.

SymExt is Salsa-interned with crate_num, def_index and kind. It contains no name, signature, fields, predicates, metadata availability, or namespace. Thus metadata facts do not participate in identity. Technically the interned tuple includes kind: pair-only identity holds under the claim's explicit consistent-provider-kind requirement, rather than through runtime rejection of arbitrary inconsistent tuples. SymExt name/children queries use the existing handle and pair to request metadata; named_children retains namespace on the resolution edge, not the handle. Symbol's external representation retains the SymExt handle. Captured lower_def likewise constructs only the pair plus kind, while captured typed metadata queries use the handle's pair and return facts separately.

The rustc adapter obtains module-child identity from the resolved child DefId and maps tcx.def_kind(child_did) with sym_ext_kind_for_def_kind; reexports and namespace variants preserve that pair/kind. The deterministic mapping distinguishes definitions and constructors and maps associated functions/types/constants consistently to Fn/TypeAlias/Const. Associated-item extraction uses those same kinds from rustc's typed associated-item category. Inherent method candidates derive Fn and Impl from typed rustc method/impl lists, relevant impl enumeration supplies Impl, trait predicates supply Trait, ADT lowering uses the same central mapping, and projection lowering supplies TypeAlias and Trait after checking its owner. These reviewed adapter paths do not select different definition kinds according to the requested metadata fact. The new implementation association makes the essential adapter source part of future review invalidation.

The only associated test, todo::symbols_external_identity, is explicitly empty and documents both remaining identity-across-metadata-update tests and inconsistent-provider-kind handling. Accepted as a genuine test deferral, not passing functional evidence: there are no substantive ordinary associated assertions establishing this anchor at runtime. Completing the update coverage requires a fixture that varies available/name/signature metadata while preserving crate/index/kind and checks handle equality before and after requests; inconsistent-provider coverage requires choosing and implementing a rejection/validation boundary before asserting rejection. No current runtime rejection is claimed. Malformed provider kinds are outside the consistent-adapter qualification, so absence of such hardening does not by itself contradict the claim. No N/A or TODO implementation entries exist and no behavioral violation in the reviewed conforming adapter paths was identified.

Source evidence was inspected independently for this anchor and relevant helper sources captured through review read. Added only an anchor association comment above the central rustc kind mapping with coordinator authorization, then ran cargo fmt and fresh-started the review. cargo build passed with warnings. No behavior suite was run by this reviewer for this assignment; root owns central tests and delegated post-codegen/Sage sanity checks. The concurrently coordinated UseSymbol wrapper correction does not change SymExt's interning fields or metadata identity model.
